questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to go to the production animal hospital and doing farm visits with the staff there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The hardest part was the Finnish language.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, University of Helsinki send out information and as a exchange student we also had tutors (whatsapp) to ask about anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Eeva at University of Helsinki gave me all the information I needed my first day. Also she was the best person to contact before and during my stay. She answered every exchange student so fast and was very willing to help out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I preferred to live by my own (since I can have problem with head ache and need peace and quiet after school) and also got a small studio apartment easily through HOAS. I could not get housing on campus through HOAS, but I know an other exchange student that got it close to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Get a month public transport ticket by HSL with student discount. Eeva helps you how to do it. I brought my car from Sweden since it was impossible for me to get to production animal hospital (70km outside Helsinki) without it and that was the reason in first place I wanted to go to Finland since Copenhagen Uni does not offer farm visits for students during clinical rotations. Helsinki University does not provide bus to Production animal hospital and the students have to go there by their own car. 
I lived in Norra Haga and was were satisfied with that area, close to forest and nature. Helsinki is a beautiful calm city with a lot of nature, so anywhere you can end up I think it will be good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for a long time ago and wanted to go to Norway but the University in Norway didnt offer a exchange period for students in 2025 which my university didnt know about (I was the one the contacted the universities). My university offered my other places to go to and I found that Finland have a production animal hospital there students can go with the vets for farm visits. I was confused for a long time if I should go since I couldnt go to Norway. Very late I decided to go and Eeva from University of Helsinki offered me a stay directly.  I think my contact person from Copenhagen was not very happy with me that I was so late but as the Finnish mentality, they was very happy to have me and I felt very welcome even though I applied late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Eeva at University of Helsinki and contact person for exchange at my university through email. They also helped me through the process with learning agreement etc. Also got a lot of information through University of Helsinki website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, wanted to follow rotation A with focus at large animal which I also did.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan your exchange in time, because everything takes a lot more time than I expected. I did manage to do everything in one semester (with forhåndsmerit etc) but it was stressful. University of Copenhagen answer email much slower then University of Helsinki so the host institution was never a problem to get everything in place in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations at the University hospitals (small animal, equine and production animal) as the most important part of veterinary medicine program. I got work and practice right beside the vets and have real own patients/cases. All from small animal internal medicine patients to surgery on a cow at a farm.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All the teachers/vets in Finland are in general much nicer, no judging and also with the mentality of learning by doing. There was also more cases to practice and follow during my stay and more focus at the practical skills rather then journal writing. I should easily question anything without a feeling as a stupid student. The equine hospital staff was so nice and since I been there I can again consider to see myself as an equine vet. The equine hospital in Copenhagen I think has scared me more than developed my skills. I think I learned more of 3 months of stay in Finland then I have a whole year of clinical rotations in Copenhagen. The Finnish students have the whole 5th years just with clinical rotation at the hospitals and only practice things besides the vets (as a example they are 6 weeks in total at production animal hospital during the year). In Copenhagen we also have lectures/courses through the clinical year and I learn more of doing the practical things.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotation/practice 
- Small animal general polyclinic
- Small animal surgery, anesthesia
- Small animal internal medicine ward
- Small animal surgery operating theatre
- Equine hospital x3 weeks 
- Production animal hospital x4 weeks

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Anesthesia week and surgery operating theatre at small animal hospital.
You have to go to Production animal hospital, you will get a experience for life. One day I had cow reproduction at a farm and we examined about 80 cows. Learned a lot! Long day without lunch but in the late afternoon we got dinner inside the farmers house with the whole family and they were very sweet to us.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lived by myself so my house rent was probably higher then if you chose to live with others. I also have my money in swedish crown so it was even more expensive for me then the numbers in Dannish crown. I think the food is expensive but probably suits well to the cost in Denmark. Wifi and electricity was included in the rent just payed for my phone. I had my own books with me that I already had bought during the beginning of my master. Books are also available in almost every ward at the hospitals.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping and also public transport fees.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The tutors organized gatherings etc for the exchange students. We also had a international dinner night which was very nice. 
I think they have sports at Uni-sport, but I found out it was cheaper for me to train at the local gym in my area so I did that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit the city center and just stroll around. The cathedral is very beautiful and in the old market hall I tasted very nice reindeer delicacy. The city is much calmer then Copenhagen but still alive with a lot of things and culture to explore, like the museums.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: One weekend I went to ski in Vithi ski center together with the other exchange students. It was a very nice and sunny day, it was quiet expensive so count on minimun 80 euro for one day of skiing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: When I arrived in January it was very much as in Sweden, people are introverted and are mostly at home. I felt very lonely and had hard to connect with the other students since the didnt talked so much with me. Later in the semester I felt that people opened up more and didnt felt scared to talk english or swedish with me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with the tutors, they are the best!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Were introverted persons as a start, also these students had know each other for more then 4 years so it wad a little bit hard to connect with them. I also think they had a lot in school and tried to survive the hardest year of vet school. Otherwise are Finnish people very nice and gently so when I just continued to talk to them it got easier and I felt that they probably are shy in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of Finnish people, no judgement and also were willing to help out if you ask them for anything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go there in the end of February or beginning of March instead, other exchange student arrive then and it was not so dark at that time. You can still get the winter experience in the beginning of your stay and be there when the spring arrive, and  also attend Vappu at the 1st of May. I left before Vappu but the Finnish student talked so much about it and it felt it was something to look forward to. 
2. Explore the Finnish nature!
3. Go to production animal hospital, the teachers are really nice there and the drive around at the Finnish country side was a experience. You can also get cheap housing through the university during you stay there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Email Eeva whenever you have a question.  I would also say that you need to have a erasmus grant to help with the costs! 
Otherwise go with the flow and just enjoy the experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Days I had alone with the farm vets. The Finnish people had exam some days so I went alone in the car with the vet. For example I treated a uterine prolapse and did teeth rasping at 10 horses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Finnish language, farmers didnt speak english or swedish and sometime vets talked a lot in Finnish with the other students. But it depends on the vet you are with, some of them only speak english (as in equine hospital).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Finland! You will learn a lot, explore beautiful nature and meet new friends!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
